title: Origins of modern banking
summary: At the start of the 14th century, merchant companies of Florence such as the Bardi and Peruzzi were well established. By 1310 the Bardi were the wealthiest family in the city. These family banks kept branches across Europe and the Middle East, took deposits from outsiders, traded commodities and lent to rulers, including Edward III of England. They collapsed around 1345.

uncertainty.note: The Bardi and Peruzzi super-companies expanded from late 13th-century money changing into transnational financial empires c. 1300 before collapsing following sovereign defaults by Edward III between 1343 and 1346.
